base.name: Capital
base.desc: Destroy the enemy capital to win. Protect yours!

rifleman.name: M4 Rifleman
rifleman.desc: Infantry. Cheap frontline infantry. Weak against armor.

assault.name: SCAR-H Assault
assault.desc: Assault infantry. Fast SMG trooper. Deadly up close, short range.

bazooka.name: Carl Gustaf Trooper
bazooka.desc: Anti-tank infantry. Anti-tank rockets. Excellent against vehicles.

mg_gunner.name: M240 Machine Gunner
mg_gunner.desc: Machine gunner. Slow but pours out suppressive fire.

grenadier.name: M320 Grenadier
grenadier.desc: Grenadier. Lobs grenades. Splash damage against groups.

sniper.name: M82 Barrett Sniper
sniper.desc: Sniper. One shot, one kill - against infantry. Useless against armor.

flamer.name: M2 Flamethrower
flamer.desc: Flamethrower trooper. Burns infantry and buildings at point-blank range.

medic.name: CLS Combat Medic
medic.desc: Medic. Heals nearby infantry. Follows the army.

commando.name: Delta Force SOF
commando.desc: Special forces. Elite operative. Armor-piercing rifle, tough and fast.

jeep.name: HMMWV Humvee
jeep.desc: Scout vehicle. Fast raider with a machine gun. Shreds infantry.

armored_car.name: LAV-25 Scout Car
armored_car.desc: Armored car. Fast recon vehicle with an autocannon.

apc.name: M2 Bradley IFV
apc.desc: Infantry fighting vehicle. Armored carrier. Unloads troops when destroyed.

heavy_tank.name: Leopard 2A7 Tank
heavy_tank.desc: Heavy main battle tank. Slow, nearly unstoppable armor.

mammoth.name: T-14 Armata Tank
mammoth.desc: Super-heavy tank. Twin-cannon super-heavy. Crushes buildings.

tank_destroyer.name: B1 Centauro TD
tank_destroyer.desc: Tank destroyer. Long-range hunter of armor. Poor against infantry.

flame_tank.name: M132 Flame Tank
flame_tank.desc: Flame tank. Short-range inferno. Melts infantry and buildings.

artillery.name: M109 Paladin SPG
artillery.desc: Self-propelled gun. Long-range splash damage. Cannot hit close targets.

howitzer.name: PzH 2000 Howitzer
howitzer.desc: Heavy howitzer. Huge range. Needs a Radar Station for spotting.

mlrs.name: M142 HIMARS
mlrs.desc: Rocket artillery. Multiple-launch rocket system: rapid area bombardment.

aa_truck.name: M1097 Avenger AA
aa_truck.desc: Mobile anti-air. Rapid-fire flak against aircraft.

sam_truck.name: Patriot PAC-3 SAM
sam_truck.desc: Mobile SAM launcher. Long-range anti-air missiles.

repair_vehicle.name: M88 Hercules ARV
repair_vehicle.desc: Recovery & repair vehicle. Repairs nearby vehicles and tanks. Follows the army.

drone.name: Switchblade Drone
drone.desc: Kamikaze drone. Cheap suicide drone. Explodes on the first ground target.

fighter.name: F-16 Fighting Falcon
fighter.desc: Multirole fighter. Fast multirole fighter. Dominates the sky.

interceptor_jet.name: F-15C Eagle
interceptor_jet.desc: Air superiority fighter. Hunts enemy aircraft only. Very fast.

stealth_fighter.name: F-22 Raptor Stealth
stealth_fighter.desc: Stealth fighter. Nearly invisible: enemies only see it at close range.

strike_jet.name: F-15E Strike Eagle
strike_jet.desc: Strike fighter. Ground-attack jet with armor-piercing cannon.

helicopter.name: AH-64E Apache
helicopter.desc: Attack helicopter. Tough gunship armed with rockets. Drops depth charges on submarines and divers.

gunship.name: AC-130J Ghostrider
gunship.desc: Heavy gunship. Flying fortress. Rockets with splash.

light_bomber.name: Su-34 Fullback
light_bomber.desc: Fighter-bomber. Fast bombing runs over the battlefield.

bomber.name: B-1B Lancer Bomber
bomber.desc: Supersonic bomber. Flies bombing runs over the battlefield. Needs anti-air cover.

heavy_bomber.name: B-52 Stratofortress
heavy_bomber.desc: Strategic bomber. Carpet-bombs everything below. Wrecks buildings.

stealth_bomber.name: B-2 Stealth Bomber
stealth_bomber.desc: Stealth bomber. Invisible until it is overhead. Devastating payload.

diver.name: Navy SEAL Diver
diver.desc: Combat diver. Frogman. Walks on land, swims unseen underwater and plants limpet mines. Deadly to ships.

patrol_boat.name: Mk VI Patrol Boat
patrol_boat.desc: Patrol boat. Fast machine-gun skiff. Sails rivers and sea. Weak against anything heavy.

gunboat.name: CB90 Assault Boat
gunboat.desc: River gunboat. Small cannon boat. Sails rivers and sea and shells coastal targets.

missile_boat.name: Hamina Missile Boat
missile_boat.desc: Missile boat. Guided rockets: strong against aircraft and ships. Needs a river or sea.

destroyer.name: Arleigh Burke DDG
destroyer.desc: Guided-missile destroyer. Versatile warship. Guns for land and air, depth charges for submarines and divers.

cruiser.name: Ticonderoga Cruiser
cruiser.desc: Guided-missile cruiser. Heavy gun cruiser. Long range, strong armor. Deep sea only.

battleship.name: USS Iowa Battleship
battleship.desc: Battleship. Huge guns that flatten coastal cities. Slow and costly. Deep sea only.

submarine.name: Virginia Class Sub
submarine.desc: Attack submarine. Submerged hunter. Torpedoes cripple ships. Only destroyers, helicopters and other subs can hit it.

aircraft_carrier.name: USS Nimitz Carrier
aircraft_carrier.desc: Aircraft carrier. Floating airbase: launches free aircraft and lets you build aircraft without an Airbase. Shoots down planes and missiles. Deep sea only.

shotgunner.name: Mossberg Breacher
shotgunner.desc: Close-quarters infantry. Devastating shotgun blasts at point-blank range, useless at distance.

marksman.name: M110 Marksman
marksman.desc: Designated marksman. Accurate mid-range rifle, strong against infantry.

mortar_team.name: M224 Mortar Team
mortar_team.desc: Indirect-fire support. Lobs mortar rounds over obstacles; cannot hit anything close.

javelin.name: FGM-148 Javelin Team
javelin.desc: Anti-tank team. Rocket or guided-missile launcher that punches through armor at range.

riot_trooper.name: Heavy Assault Trooper
riot_trooper.desc: Heavily armored shock infantry. Very tough, short-ranged. Soaks damage for the squad.

sapper.name: Combat Sapper
sapper.desc: Combat engineer. Lays anti-tank mines as it advances and safely clears enemy minefields.

officer.name: Squad Commander
officer.desc: Field officer. Nearby friendly units fire 25% harder. Follows the troops.

k9.name: K9 Demolition Dog
k9.desc: Fast explosive-laden dog. Sprints at the enemy and detonates.

mine_flail.name: Mine Flail Tank
mine_flail.desc: Mine-clearing armor. Flails or rolls through minefields, defusing every mine and trap near it, with a light MG.

torpedo_boat.name: PT Torpedo Boat
torpedo_boat.desc: Fast attack boat. Launches torpedoes that only hit things in the water. Deadly to ships.

frigate.name: ASW Frigate
frigate.desc: Anti-submarine frigate. Guns for land and air, depth charges for subs and divers.

minelayer.name: Minelayer
minelayer.desc: Sows naval mines as it sails. Mines sink ships and subs that wander into them.

midget_sub.name: Midget Submarine
midget_sub.desc: Tiny stealth submarine. Hard to spot; one torpedo can cripple a ship.

cruise_sub.name: Ohio-class SSGN
cruise_sub.desc: Missile submarine. Launches long-range missiles at land and sea targets from hiding.

pillbox.name: Hardened Pillbox
pillbox.desc: Pillbox. Concrete machine-gun nest. Hard to kill.

at_gun.name: TOW-2 AT Emplacement
at_gun.desc: Anti-tank emplacement. Armor-piercing gun. Deadly to tanks.

cannon_turret.name: M68 105mm Bunker
cannon_turret.desc: Cannon bunker. Armored bunker with a heavy cannon.

mortar_pit.name: M252 Mortar Pit
mortar_pit.desc: Mortar pit. Indirect fire over walls. Cannot hit close targets.

flak_battery.name: Oerlikon Skynex Flak
flak_battery.desc: Flak battery. Airburst flak shreds groups of aircraft.

sam_site.name: NASAMS SAM Site
sam_site.desc: SAM site. Surface-to-air missiles. Needs power; radar extends its range.

heavy_battery.name: M777 155mm Battery
heavy_battery.desc: Heavy artillery battery. Fixed long-range artillery battery.

railgun.name: ONR EMRG Railgun
railgun.desc: Railgun battery. Hyper-velocity gun. Pierces any armor. Needs power.

ciws.name: Mk 15 Phalanx CIWS
ciws.desc: Close-in weapon system. Rapid-fire point defense against aircraft and missiles. Needs power.

interceptor_battery.name: Iron Dome Battery
interceptor_battery.desc: Missile interceptor. Shoots down incoming missiles and nukes. Needs power; radar extends range.

abm_battery.name: THAAD ABM Battery
abm_battery.desc: Anti-ballistic missile battery. Long-range anti-ballistic system. Double-strength interceptors.

barricade.name: Jersey Barrier
barricade.desc: Barricade. Cheap wall that soaks up fire.

repair_depot.name: Field Repair Depot
repair_depot.desc: Repair depot. Repairs friendly vehicles and buildings nearby. Needs power.

coastal_battery.name: NSM Coastal Battery
coastal_battery.desc: Coastal defense battery. Shore gun that only fires at ships, subs and divers in the water. Build near the coast.

sandbag_nest.name: Sandbag MG Nest
sandbag_nest.desc: Cheap sandbagged machine-gun nest. Good value against infantry.

watchtower.name: Watchtower
watchtower.desc: Tall wooden tower with a long-range rifle post. Weak armor.

sniper_nest.name: Sniper Nest
sniper_nest.desc: Hidden sniper post. Kills infantry at long range, useless against armor.

flame_bunker.name: Flamethrower Bunker
flame_bunker.desc: Fortified flamethrower pit. Roasts infantry and light vehicles that get close.

torpedo_battery.name: Shore Torpedo Battery
torpedo_battery.desc: Coastal torpedo tubes. Only fires at ships and subs in the water. Build near the coast.

observation_post.name: Observation Post
observation_post.desc: Spotter tower. All friendly units and defenses within range fire 20% harder.

landmine.name: Anti-Tank Mine
landmine.desc: Buried mine. Detonates under vehicles; infantry are too light to trigger it. Hidden from view of the enemy until it goes off.

ap_mine.name: Anti-Personnel Mine
ap_mine.desc: Cheap mine that shreds infantry. Vehicles roll over it safely.

claymore.name: Claymore Array
claymore.desc: Directional charges with a wide trigger area. Lethal to infantry that walk into the kill zone.

napalm_trap.name: Napalm Trap
napalm_trap.desc: Buried fuel drums. Explodes in a huge fireball when enemy ground units approach.

barbed_wire.name: Barbed Wire
barbed_wire.desc: Entangles infantry: slows them a lot and cuts them slowly.

tank_trap.name: Dragon's Teeth
tank_trap.desc: Concrete tank traps. Vehicles crawl through them.

naval_mine.name: Naval Mine
naval_mine.desc: Moored sea mine. Sinks ships and subs that touch it. Deploy in your own waters.

decoy_tank.name: Inflatable Decoy Tank
decoy_tank.desc: Looks like a real tank from afar. Enemy units waste ammunition on it.

oil_refinery.name: Oil Refinery
oil_refinery.desc: +3 income per second. Explodes when destroyed.

power_plant.name: Power Plant
power_plant.desc: Powers SAMs, interceptors, railguns, CIWS and radars.

barracks.name: Barracks
barracks.desc: Unlocks elite infantry and trains free troops.

factory.name: War Factory
factory.desc: Unlocks heavy vehicles and builds free light vehicles.

airbase.name: Airbase
airbase.desc: Required for all aircraft. Scrambles free drones and fighters.

radar_station.name: Radar Station
radar_station.desc: Extends SAM and interceptor range. Spots for howitzers.

missile_silo.name: Missile Silo
missile_silo.desc: Required for ballistic missiles and nukes. Launches from here.

tech_center.name: Tech Center
tech_center.desc: Unlocks stealth aircraft, super-heavy armor, ABMs and doomsday weapons.

fortress.name: Fortress
fortress.desc: Massive stronghold with a heavy cannon.

naval_port.name: Naval Port
naval_port.desc: Unlocks boats, ships and subs. Must be on the coast. Launches free patrol boats and gunboats.

field_hospital.name: Field Hospital
field_hospital.desc: Heals wounded infantry nearby. Keeps your troops in the fight.

fuel_depot.name: Fuel Depot
fuel_depot.desc: Bulk fuel storage: +2 income. Explodes violently when destroyed!

forward_base.name: Forward Operating Base
forward_base.desc: Fortified outpost that can be built far forward. Acts as a Barracks, trains free troops and has its own gun.

tactical_missile.name: M39 ATACMS
tactical_missile.desc: Tactical missile. Cheap and quick. Light blast.

cruise_missile.name: BGM-109 Tomahawk
cruise_missile.desc: Cruise missile. Fast, precise and cheap. Easy for interceptors to kill (1 hit).

cluster_missile.name: Iskander-M Cluster
cluster_missile.desc: Cluster missile. Wide blast: great against massed troops.

bunker_buster.name: GBU-57 Bunker Buster
bunker_buster.desc: Bunker buster. Pierces armor. Triple damage against buildings.

ballistic_missile.name: Pershing II Missile
ballistic_missile.desc: Ballistic missile. Heavy warhead that wipes out clusters. Needs 2 interceptor hits.

hypersonic.name: Kh-47M2 Kinzhal
hypersonic.desc: Hypersonic missile. Brutally fast. Almost no time to react.

tactical_nuke.name: B61 Tactical Nuke
tactical_nuke.desc: Tactical nuke. A smaller nuclear warhead. Erases a city block.

nuke.name: LGM-30 Minuteman III
nuke.desc: Nuclear ICBM. Devastating. Obliterates everything in a huge radius. Needs 3 interceptor hits.

mega_nuke.name: RDS-220 Tsar Bomba
mega_nuke.desc: Doomsday device. Annihilates an entire region. The end of the world.

wehrmacht.name: Wehrmacht
wehrmacht.desc: Combined-arms Wehrmacht of 1944: superb optics and long-range guns, but few vehicles built at great cost. Tech slots hold Luftwaffe jets and wonder weapons; the nuclear slots are what-ifs, as Germany never built a bomb.

blitzkrieg.name: Blitzkrieg
blitzkrieg.desc: Fast armor and Stukas hit before you can dig in. Starts with a panzer spearhead.

westwall.name: Westwall
westwall.desc: Concrete, flak and 88s. Starts with a fortified front line.

wunderwaffen.name: Wunderwaffen
wunderwaffen.desc: Rockets and experimental superweapons, built cheap and fired often.

rifleman.name: Kar98k Schuetze
rifleman.desc: Standard German infantry rifle: accurate and sturdy, but its five-round bolt action fires slowly compared with later self-loaders.

assault.name: StG 44 Sturmmann
assault.desc: First mass-produced assault rifle. Intermediate cartridge gives SMG handling with rifle range; arrived too late and in too small numbers.

bazooka.name: Panzerschreck Team
bazooka.desc: 88 mm reloadable rocket launcher with a shaped-charge warhead, copied from the US bazooka. Short effective range and a back-blast.

manpads.name: MG 34 AA Gunner
manpads.desc: MG 34 on a tripod in the air-defence role. Can pester low-flying aircraft but cannot stop armored ground-attack planes.

mg_gunner.name: MG 42 Gunner
mg_gunner.desc: Fires 1,200 rounds per minute with a characteristic tearing sound; the pattern for modern GPMGs.

grenadier.name: Sturmpionier
grenadier.desc: Stick grenades, satchel charges and flamethrower training for clearing bunkers and trenches.

sniper.name: Kar98k ZF39 Scharfschuetze
sniper.desc: Kar98k with 1.5x ZF39 scope, selected for accuracy. Kills at 600 m but is slow to fire.

flamer.name: Flammenwerfer 41
flamer.desc: Man-portable flamethrower with 7 L of fuel and 25-35 m range for about 10 seconds. Terrifying vs bunkers, lethal to carry.

medic.name: Sanitaeter
medic.desc: Unarmed medic with a bag of dressings and morphine; red cross armband is not always respected.

engineer.name: Pionier
engineer.desc: Builds bridges, clears mines and demolishes obstacles; also fights as infantry when needed.

commando.name: Fallschirmjaeger FG 42
commando.desc: Luftwaffe paratroopers armed with the FG 42 automatic rifle. Elite training, but few survive Crete-style losses.

jeep.name: Kuebelwagen
jeep.desc: VW Type 82 with air-cooled flat-four; light, simple and cheap. Unarmored and only lightly armed.

armored_car.name: Sd.Kfz. 234/2 Puma
armored_car.desc: Eight-wheeled reconnaissance car with a 50 mm KwK 39/1, one of the best of the war. Fast and quiet but thinly armored.

apc.name: Sd.Kfz. 251 Hanomag
apc.desc: Carries ten grenadiers with a front MG 34 and rear MG 42. Open-topped, so vulnerable to artillery airbursts.

light_tank.name: Panzer III Ausf. N
light_tank.desc: Reworked Panzer III with a short 75 mm gun for infantry support; outclassed but numerous.

tank.name: Panzer IV Ausf. H
tank.desc: Reliable workhorse with a long 75 mm KwK 40 gun and Schuerzen skirts. Outgunned by the T-34-85 and IS-2 but widely produced.

heavy_tank.name: Tiger II (Koenigstiger)
heavy_tank.desc: 68-ton tank with a 88 mm KwK 43 L/71 and 150 mm sloped front armor. Nearly impenetrable from the front, short on range and fuel.

mammoth.name: Panzer VIII Maus
mammoth.desc: 188-ton prototype with a 128 mm KwK 44 and 200 mm front armor. Only two were built; the engine could not move it fast.

tank_destroyer.name: Jagdpanther
tank_destroyer.desc: Panther chassis with 8.8 cm PaK 43 L/71 in a fixed casemate. One of the best anti-tank vehicles of the war.

flame_tank.name: Flammpanzer III
flame_tank.desc: Panzer III with a Flammenwerfer in the turret. Short range but destroys bunkers and infantry in cover.

artillery.name: Wespe SPG
artillery.desc: 10.5 cm leFH 18/2 gun on a Panzer II chassis. Thin armor but mobile enough to keep up with panzer units.

howitzer.name: Hummel (15 cm sFH 18)
howitzer.desc: 15 cm heavy field howitzer on a Panzer III/IV chassis; one of the strongest mobile artillery pieces.

mlrs.name: Panzerwerfer 42 Maultier
mlrs.desc: Ten-barrel 15 cm rocket launcher on a half-track; fires in seconds and then relocates.

aa_truck.name: Wirbelwind Flakpanzer
aa_truck.desc: Panzer IV hull with a quad 20 mm Flakvierling in an open turret. Highly effective against low aircraft and infantry.

sam_truck.name: Sd.Kfz. 7 8.8 cm Flak
sam_truck.desc: The famous 88 mounted on a half-track; fires at altitudes up to 8,000 m and doubles as anti-tank gun.

repair_vehicle.name: Bergepanther ARV
repair_vehicle.desc: Panther chassis with a winch and crane; recovered tanks under fire and returned them to workshops.

drone.name: Mistel S2 Composite
drone.desc: Obsolete Ju 88 loaded with a 3.8 t hollow-charge warhead and guided into the target by an Fw 190 mounted on top.

fighter.name: Bf 109 G-6
fighter.desc: Main Luftwaffe fighter with a 20 mm cannon and two MG 131s. Small and agile but short on range.

interceptor_jet.name: Fw 190 A-8
interceptor_jet.desc: Radial-engine fighter with four 20 mm cannons and armor plate; the Sturmbock variant was made to shoot down bombers.

stealth_fighter.name: Me 262 A-1a Schwalbe
stealth_fighter.desc: First operational jet fighter, with four 30 mm MK 108 cannons; 150 km/h faster than any Allied fighter. Unreliable engines.

strike_jet.name: Ju 87 G Stuka
strike_jet.desc: Stuka fitted with two 37 mm BK 3.7 cannon; Hans-Ulrich Rudel destroyed over 500 tanks with the type.

helicopter.name: Fl 282 Kolibri
helicopter.desc: Synchropter used for convoy spotting and anti-submarine patrol; only about 24 were built and none carried real firepower.

gunship.name: Hs 129 B-3
gunship.desc: Twin-engine attack plane armoured against small arms; the B-3 carried a 7.5 cm BK 7.5 cannon. About 25 were built.

light_bomber.name: Ju 88 A-4
light_bomber.desc: Fast, versatile twin-engine bomber also used as dive bomber and night fighter.

bomber.name: He 111 H-6
bomber.desc: Glass-nosed twin-engine bomber, vulnerable to fighters after the Battle of Britain.

heavy_bomber.name: He 177 A-5 Greif
heavy_bomber.desc: Four-engine bomber with two coupled engines; the tendency to catch fire limited its usefulness.

stealth_bomber.name: Horten Ho 229
stealth_bomber.desc: Jet flying wing with possible radar-absorbing glue; only prototypes flew. Modelled as a small stealthy bomber.

diver.name: Kampfschwimmer
diver.desc: Naval commandos using limpet mines against bridges and ships; trained late in the war at Venice.

patrol_boat.name: S-100 Schnellboot
patrol_boat.desc: Diesel-powered S-boats dashed at 40 knots to hit coastal convoys with torpedoes and 20 mm guns.

gunboat.name: Siebel Ferry Gunboat
gunboat.desc: Catamaran ferry fitted with 88 mm guns and flak; invasion barge converted to river and coastal defence.

missile_boat.name: T-24 Torpedoboot
missile_boat.desc: Type 39 torpedo boat with four 10.5 cm guns and six torpedo tubes; larger than a destroyer escort.

destroyer.name: Z-31 (Zerstoerer 1936A)
destroyer.desc: Large 3,000-ton destroyer with five 15 cm guns, ill-suited to rough seas. Fast but short-ranged.

cruiser.name: Admiral Hipper
cruiser.desc: Eight 20.3 cm guns, 14,000 t. Bold raider with poor reliability from high-pressure steam plants.

battleship.name: Bismarck
battleship.desc: Eight 38 cm guns and heavy armor. Sank HMS Hood in 1941 before being hunted down; the Kriegsmarine's only real peer to the Allies.

submarine.name: U-boat Type XXI
submarine.desc: Streamlined with huge batteries; 17 knots submerged. Revolutionised submarine design but entered service in 1945.

aircraft_carrier.name: Graf Zeppelin
aircraft_carrier.desc: Launched in 1938 but never completed; planned for 40 aircraft. In game it carries a mixed, slow-cycling air group.

mg_turret.name: MG 42 Nest
mg_turret.desc: Stellung with MG 42 and interlocking arcs of fire; a few well-sited guns can halt a battalion.

pillbox.name: Westwall Regelbau
pillbox.desc: Standard design from the Siegfried Line: reinforced concrete up to 2 m thick, with MG embrasures.

at_gun.name: PaK 40 7.5 cm
at_gun.desc: Excellent 75 mm gun that could defeat most Allied tanks at 1,000 m; heavy to relocate.

cannon_turret.name: Panther-Turm Stellung
cannon_turret.desc: Panther turret set on a concrete base; used on the Atlantic Wall and in Italy as a cheap, well-armored gun.

mortar_pit.name: GrW 34 8 cm Mortar
mortar_pit.desc: Standard German 81 mm mortar with 2,400 m range; high rate of fire for its time.

flak_battery.name: 3.7 cm Flak 36/37
flak_battery.desc: Automatic 37 mm gun; reasonable against low aircraft but short-ranged.

sam_site.name: 8.8 cm Flak 36/37
sam_site.desc: The 88: 8.8 cm shells up to 10 km. Excellent against aircraft and tanks alike.

heavy_battery.name: Batterie Todt 38 cm
heavy_battery.desc: Four 38 cm SK C/34 guns from the Atlantic Wall; capable of striking targets across the Channel.

railgun.name: 80 cm Schwerer Gustav
railgun.desc: Largest-calibre gun ever used in combat: 80 cm, shell 7.1 t. Only two built; used at Sevastopol 1942.

ciws.name: Flakvierling 38
ciws.desc: Four 20 mm Flak 38 on one mount; 1,800 rpm for a hail of fire against low aircraft.

interceptor_battery.name: Wasserfall SAM
interceptor_battery.desc: Radio-guided liquid-fuel SAM; 35 flight tests but never fielded. Modelled as the Reich's missile screen.

abm_battery.name: Enzian SAM Battery
abm_battery.desc: Me 163-derived rocket-powered SAM. A paper project; no German system could actually hit a ballistic missile.

barricade.name: Tschechenigel Hedgehog
barricade.desc: Welded steel beams that stop tanks; used on beaches and in streets.

repair_depot.name: Feldwerkstatt
repair_depot.desc: Mobile Kfz workshop that repairs vehicles and weapons close behind the front.

coastal_battery.name: 15 cm Kuestenbatterie
coastal_battery.desc: 15 cm TbK C/36 guns in open casemates for the Atlantic Wall; 22 km range vs ships.

tactical_missile.name: Rheinbote
tactical_missile.desc: Four-stage solid rocket with a 40 kg warhead; 160 km range but poor accuracy. Used against Antwerp in 1944-45.

cruise_missile.name: Fi 103 (V-1)
cruise_missile.desc: Pulse-jet cruise missile with a 850 kg warhead; 250 km range, shot down by fighters and flak.

cluster_missile.name: 15 cm Nebelwerfer Salvo
cluster_missile.desc: Barrage of six-barrel Nebelwerfers; saturates a zone with HE.

bunker_buster.name: PC 1400 X (Fritz X)
bunker_buster.desc: Radio-controlled armor-piercing bomb that sank the battleship Roma in 1943; the first precision guided munition used in combat.

ballistic_missile.name: A4 (V-2)
ballistic_missile.desc: First long-range ballistic missile; 1 t of amatol and 320 km range. Nothing could stop it.

hypersonic.name: A9/A10 Amerika-Rakete
hypersonic.desc: Paper project for a two-stage rocket to reach New York; never built.

tactical_nuke.name: Uranbombe
tactical_nuke.desc: Never built; what-if weapon. The wartime Uranverein never got beyond experimental reactors.

nuke.name: A10 Uran-Rakete
nuke.desc: Never built; what-if weapon. Modelled as a V-2 follow-on carrying an atomic payload.

mega_nuke.name: Wunderwaffe Zero
mega_nuke.desc: Never built; what-if weapon. Pure fiction; included to keep the match balanced.

red_army.name: Red Army
red_army.tagline: Quantity has a quality all its own.
red_army.desc: Soviet mass mobilisation: simple, rugged and plentiful. Cheap infantry, rocket artillery and sloped-armor tanks. Aircraft are rugged ground-attackers, there is no carrier and the tech slots hold early post-war jets and the first Soviet bombs.

deep_battle.name: Deep Battle
deep_battle.desc: Massed artillery and Katyushas soften the line. Starts with a rocket park.

human_wave.name: Human Wave
human_wave.desc: Endless cheap riflemen. Starts with a huge infantry horde.

kursk.name: Kursk Salient
kursk.desc: Layered anti-tank belts. Starts with AT guns, pillboxes and mortars.

rifleman.name: Mosin M91/30 Rifleman
rifleman.desc: Simple, very rugged Russian rifle with a bayonet; made in the tens of millions.

assault.name: PPSh-41 SMG Trooper
assault.desc: 71-round drum and 900 rpm made it a favourite of storm groups; short range but cheap to mass produce.

bazooka.name: PTRD-41 AT Rifleman
bazooka.desc: Single-shot 14.5 mm rifle; could penetrate light tanks but was ineffective against 1944-class armor.

manpads.name: DShK AA Gunner
manpads.desc: 12.7 mm DShK on a wheeled AA mount; ok against low-flying aircraft.

mg_gunner.name: DP-27 Machine Gunner
mg_gunner.desc: 47-round pan magazine fed from above, simple and reliable; lower rate than the MG 42.

grenadier.name: RGD-33 Grenadier
grenadier.desc: Hand-thrown fragmentation grenades supplemented by rifle-grenade launchers.

sniper.name: Mosin PU Sniper
sniper.desc: Top-scoring snipers of the war, including those at Stalingrad; rifle with 3.5x PU scope.

flamer.name: ROKS-3 Flamethrower
flamer.desc: 23 kg backpack flamethrower; used by dedicated assault teams to clear bunkers.

medic.name: Sanitar Medic
medic.desc: Female medics (sanitarkas) carried wounded off the battlefield in large numbers.

engineer.name: Sapper Engineer
engineer.desc: Assault engineer-sapper battalions cleared mines and obstacles ahead of the infantry.

commando.name: Razvedchik Scout
commando.desc: Divisional recon soldiers with SMGs and grenades who raid and capture prisoners behind the lines.

jeep.name: GAZ-67B Scout Car
jeep.desc: Soviet equivalent of the Jeep; open body, 54 hp engine, lightly armed.

armored_car.name: BA-64B Armored Car
armored_car.desc: Small four-wheel armored car with a DT machine gun; 3,500 built, used as scouts and staff cars.

apc.name: M3 Half-Track (Lend-Lease)
apc.desc: US-supplied M3 carrying 13 men with .50 cal; thousands arrived through the Persian corridor.

light_tank.name: T-70 Light Tank
light_tank.desc: Light tank with 45 mm gun, 60 mm front armor and low silhouette; withdrawn by 1944.

tank.name: T-34-85
tank.desc: Sloped-armor, wide-track medium tank with an 85 mm gun; the most-built tank of the war.

heavy_tank.name: IS-2 Heavy Tank
heavy_tank.desc: 122 mm D-25T gun with high-explosive punch; thick sloped armor but slow reload (about 2 rpm).

mammoth.name: IS-7 Heavy Tank
mammoth.desc: 1948 prototype: 68 t, 130 mm gun, 150 mm sloped armor and 60 km/h. Six were built; the project was cancelled.

tank_destroyer.name: SU-100 Tank Destroyer
tank_destroyer.desc: T-34 chassis with a casemate and 100 mm D-10S gun; simple, deadly and cheap.

flame_tank.name: OT-34 Flame Tank
flame_tank.desc: T-34 with an ATO-41 flamethrower in place of the bow MG; 100 m range.

artillery.name: SU-122
artillery.desc: T-34 hull with a 122 mm M-30 howitzer; a self-propelled infantry support and indirect-fire weapon.

howitzer.name: ISU-152 Zveroboy
howitzer.desc: IS chassis with a 152 mm ML-20S gun-howitzer; nicknamed 'Beast Killer' as it could knock turrets off Tigers.

mlrs.name: BM-13 Katyusha
mlrs.desc: Sixteen 132 mm rockets on a truck, fired in seven seconds. Stalin's Organ; inaccurate but psychologically devastating.

aa_truck.name: SU-37 Mobile AA
aa_truck.desc: SU-76 chassis with a 37 mm 61-K; protects columns from aircraft.

sam_truck.name: M17 MGMC AA Truck
sam_truck.desc: US-built half-track with quad .50 cal turret, supplied under Lend-Lease.

repair_vehicle.name: T-34T Recovery Tank
repair_vehicle.desc: T-34 chassis with a winch and a lifting boom.

drone.name: TB-3 Radio Drone
drone.desc: Obsolete TB-3 bomber converted to carry 3 tons of explosives and guided by radio from a mother plane; limited trials.

fighter.name: Yak-9 Fighter
fighter.desc: Light, agile fighter armed with 20 mm and 12.7 mm guns. Main Soviet fighter of 1944.

interceptor_jet.name: La-7 Interceptor
interceptor_jet.desc: Fast radial-engine fighter with three 20 mm cannons. Used by top aces like Kozhedub.

stealth_fighter.name: Yak-15
stealth_fighter.desc: First Soviet jet-powered fighter (1946), a Yak-3 fuselage with a captured German turbojet.

strike_jet.name: Il-2m3 Sturmovik
strike_jet.desc: Flying tank with 700 kg of armor, 23 mm cannon, rockets and bombs; 36,000 built, Stalin's favourite plane.

helicopter.name: Mi-1 Helicopter
helicopter.desc: Early Soviet helicopter (1948) used for observation and casualty evacuation; only experimentally armed.

gunship.name: Il-10 Sturmovik
gunship.desc: Improved Il-2 with better armor and speed; 2 x 23 mm cannon and 600 kg of bombs.

light_bomber.name: Pe-2 Dive Bomber
light_bomber.desc: Fast twin-engine dive bomber (1,000 kg load) that doubled as a reconnaissance plane.

bomber.name: Tu-2 Bomber
bomber.desc: Twin-engine bomber with 3 t load and good defensive armament; excellent but built in smaller numbers.

heavy_bomber.name: Pe-8 Heavy Bomber
heavy_bomber.desc: Rare four-engine bomber; a few carried a 5-t FAB-5000 on raids against Berlin and Helsinki.

stealth_bomber.name: Tu-4 Bull
stealth_bomber.desc: Reverse-engineered B-29 (1947) built from three interned US aircraft; Soviet nuclear delivery platform.

diver.name: Black Sea Frogman
diver.desc: Naval Spetsnaz divers began operating in 1944; mines and sabotage of ships in port.

patrol_boat.name: G-5 Torpedo Boat
patrol_boat.desc: Small, fast planing boat of 17 t with two 533 mm torpedoes; 50 knots.

gunboat.name: BK-1124 Armored Boat
gunboat.desc: Armored river boat with T-34 turret and 76 mm gun; many served on the Danube and Dnieper.

missile_boat.name: Komsomolets Torpedo Boat
missile_boat.desc: Fast patrol craft with two torpedoes and 12.7 mm guns; small but numerous.

destroyer.name: Gnevny Destroyer
destroyer.desc: Project 7 destroyer with four 130 mm guns and 38 knots; 29 built before the war.

cruiser.name: Kirov-class Cruiser
cruiser.desc: Soviet 9,000 t cruiser with nine 180 mm guns in three triple turrets; Italian-designed.

battleship.name: Sovetsky Soyuz (Project 23)
battleship.desc: Planned 59,000 t battleship with nine 406 mm guns; hulls were laid down 1938-40 but never completed.

submarine.name: Shchuka (Shch) Submarine
submarine.desc: Shch-class Pike-class boat with six bow tubes; slow submerged but cheap.

mg_turret.name: Maxim M1910 Nest
mg_turret.desc: Water-cooled Maxim on Sokolov wheeled mount; heavy but exceptionally reliable.

pillbox.name: DOT Pillbox
pillbox.desc: Long-term fire point of the Stalin Line: reinforced concrete with interlocking machine guns.

at_gun.name: ZiS-3 76 mm Gun
at_gun.desc: Cheap, effective 76.2 mm field and anti-tank gun; over 100,000 made.

cannon_turret.name: T-34 Turret Bunker
cannon_turret.desc: T-34 turret with 85 mm D-5T dug in on a concrete base; common in the Kursk defenses.

mortar_pit.name: 82 mm PM-37 Mortar
mortar_pit.desc: Company-level mortar with ranges up to 3 km; very widely used.

flak_battery.name: 61-K 37 mm AA Gun
flak_battery.desc: Soviet 37 mm automatic AA gun, a copy of the Bofors; quick-firing.

sam_site.name: 52-K 85 mm AA Gun
sam_site.desc: 85 mm medium AA gun for protecting cities; reaches 10 km.

heavy_battery.name: ML-20 152 mm Battery
heavy_battery.desc: Gun-howitzer that doubled as the ISU-152 weapon; strikes up to 17 km.

railgun.name: TM-3-12 305 mm Railway Gun
railgun.desc: Soviet railway artillery, 305 mm guns on rail carriages, used in the defense of Leningrad.

ciws.name: Maxim Quad AA
ciws.desc: Four Maxim machine guns on a mount for anti-aircraft work.

interceptor_battery.name: KS-18 85 mm Barrage
interceptor_battery.desc: Radar-directed 85 mm guns create a barrage; the best the era had against V-weapons.

abm_battery.name: KS-30 130 mm Heavy AA
abm_battery.desc: Late-war 130 mm AA gun reaching 20 km; effective only in massed barrage use.

barricade.name: Dragon's Teeth
barricade.desc: Concrete pyramids that stop tanks; widely used on the Mannerheim and Stalin lines.

repair_depot.name: Frontline Repair Base
repair_depot.desc: Mobile base repairing damaged tanks close to the front.

coastal_battery.name: B-13 130 mm Coastal Battery
coastal_battery.desc: Naval 130 mm guns in fixed coastal batteries guarding the Black Sea and Baltic.

tactical_missile.name: M-13 Rocket Barrage
tactical_missile.desc: Massed Katyusha batteries fired at once saturate a target zone.

cruise_missile.name: 10Kh Flying Bomb
cruise_missile.desc: Soviet copy of the German V-1 tested 1944-45; 900 kg warhead.

cluster_missile.name: M-30 Rocket Salvo
cluster_missile.desc: 300 mm rockets with 29 kg HE warhead for destroying fortifications.

bunker_buster.name: FAB-5000 Bomb
bunker_buster.desc: 5 t high-explosive bomb dropped by Pe-8 against Helsinki and Berlin.

ballistic_missile.name: R-1 Rocket
ballistic_missile.desc: Soviet copy of the V-2 (1948) built by Korolev's team; 270 km range.

hypersonic.name: R-2 Rocket
hypersonic.desc: R-2 extended the V-2 design to 600 km with a detachable warhead.

tactical_nuke.name: RDS-1 'Joe-1'
tactical_nuke.desc: Copy of the Fat Man implosion design tested 29 Aug 1949; 22 kt yield.

nuke.name: RDS-37 Thermonuclear
nuke.desc: First true Soviet two-stage thermonuclear weapon, tested 1955; 1.6 Mt.

mega_nuke.name: RDS-220 Tsar Bomba
mega_nuke.desc: The largest nuclear device ever tested: 50 Mt in 1961 (it was a halved 100 Mt design).

ija.name: Imperial Japanese Army
ija.desc: Imperial Army and Navy of the Pacific War: fanatical, well-trained infantry, cave and island fortresses and suicide weapons, but light tanks and few resources. The Combined Fleet lends its ships; the nuclear slots are what-ifs from the Ni-Go and F-Go projects.

banzai.name: Banzai Charge
banzai.desc: Fast, cheap, fanatical infantry. Starts with a screaming horde.

island_fortress.name: Island Fortress
island_fortress.desc: Tunnels and cave pillboxes. Starts with a hardened front and coastal guns.

combined_fleet.name: Combined Fleet
combined_fleet.desc: Lean on the navy. Starts with warships in your waters.

rifleman.name: Type 99 Rifleman
rifleman.desc: Arisaka rifle in 7.7 mm: light, accurate and reliable but a slow-firing bolt action. Standard from 1939.

assault.name: Type 100 SMG Trooper
assault.desc: Japanese SMG with a 30-round curved magazine; fewer than 10,000 built, issued to paratroopers and marines.

bazooka.name: Type 4 70 mm AT Rocket
bazooka.desc: Copy of the US bazooka developed in 1945; a few units fielded before surrender. Used with the Lunge mine and Type 99 hand mine.

manpads.name: Type 92 AA Gunner
manpads.desc: 7.7 mm Type 92 heavy machine gun on an AA tripod; good against dive bombers, little against armor.

mg_gunner.name: Type 96 LMG Gunner
mg_gunner.desc: Magazine-fed 6.5 mm LMG with a telescopic sight; cumbersome to carry but accurate.

grenadier.name: Type 89 Knee Mortar
grenadier.desc: 50 mm light grenade launcher fired from the ground; quick-reaction support for the infantry squad.

sniper.name: Type 97 Sniper
sniper.desc: 6.5 mm Arisaka with 2.5x scope; Japanese snipers in the jungle tied down units for days.

flamer.name: Type 93 Flamethrower
flamer.desc: 25 kg backpack flamethrower; used by engineers against enemy foxholes and pillboxes.

medic.name: Army Medic
medic.desc: Medics with limited supplies; the army had few doctors and no penicillin.

engineer.name: Army Engineer
engineer.desc: Engineers built bunkers and tunnels; Japan's cave defenses were mostly dug by hand.

commando.name: Giretsu Raider
commando.desc: Airborne commandos with demolition charges sent to destroy aircraft on American-held airfields.

jeep.name: Type 95 Kurogane
jeep.desc: Light 4x4 'Kurogane' scout car with an air-cooled V-twin engine; the Japanese 'Jeep'.

armored_car.name: Sumida Type 2593
armored_car.desc: Light 6-wheeled armored car used for patrol and escort duty; weakly armed with MGs.

apc.name: Ho-Ha Half-Track
apc.desc: Armored half-track carrying 14 troops; only about 100 built.

light_tank.name: Type 95 Ha-Go
light_tank.desc: Light tank with a 37 mm gun and 12 mm armor, outclassed by 1942.

tank.name: Type 97 Chi-Ha
tank.desc: Japan's most numerous tank; 47 mm gun and 25 mm armor. Diesel-powered but thin and underpowered by 1944.

heavy_tank.name: Type 4 Chi-To
heavy_tank.desc: 1944 design with a 75 mm gun and 75 mm front armor; two built before surrender.

mammoth.name: O-I Super Heavy Tank
mammoth.desc: Planned 100+ ton tank with three turrets and a 105 mm gun; only a mock-up or incomplete prototype is believed to have existed.

tank_destroyer.name: Type 3 Ho-Ni III
tank_destroyer.desc: Chi-Ha hull with a 75 mm Type 3 gun in an open-topped shield; best Japanese tank killer, 31 produced.

flame_tank.name: Chi-Ha Flamethrower Tank
flame_tank.desc: Chi-Ha with a flame projector replacing the hull MG; only prototypes were built.

artillery.name: Type 4 Ho-Ro SPG
artillery.desc: Chi-Ha chassis with a 15 cm Type 38 howitzer; heavy firepower on a light chassis, only 25 built.

howitzer.name: Type 45 24 cm Howitzer
howitzer.desc: Old 240 mm siege gun used at Port Arthur in 1904 and later as fixed heavy artillery; needs a railway or tractors.

mlrs.name: Type 4 20 cm Rocket Launcher
mlrs.desc: Single-tube spigot launcher for 20 cm rockets; used on Iwo Jima and Okinawa from caves.

aa_truck.name: Type 98 20 mm AA Truck
aa_truck.desc: Twin 20 mm AA cannon on a truck; common air defense for airfields.

sam_truck.name: Ta-Se Anti-Aircraft Tank
sam_truck.desc: Chi-Ha chassis with twin 20 mm cannon; a prototype built in 1944.

repair_vehicle.name: Type 98 So-Ki Recovery Vehicle
repair_vehicle.desc: Light recovery and engineer vehicle with winch.

drone.name: MXY-7 Ohka
drone.desc: Dropped from a Betty bomber, the Ohka dived at 800 km/h with a 1,200 kg warhead; pilots did not survive.

fighter.name: Ki-43 Hayabusa
fighter.desc: Agile with long range, but with only two 12.7 mm MGs and little armor. Called Oscar by the Allies.

interceptor_jet.name: Ki-84 Hayate
interceptor_jet.desc: One of the best Japanese fighters, carrying two 20 mm and two 12.7 mm guns; reliability suffered from fuel and parts quality.

stealth_fighter.name: J8M Shusui
stealth_fighter.desc: Licence-built Me 163; rocket motor gave 30-minute engine duration but exploded often. One flew in July 1945.

strike_jet.name: Ki-51 Sonia
strike_jet.desc: Light ground-attack aircraft with 12.7 mm MGs and small bombs; used for close air support in China.

helicopter.name: Ka-1 Autogyro
helicopter.desc: Army autogyro that took off from escort carriers to hunt submarines with two 30 kg depth charges.

gunship.name: Ki-102b Randy
gunship.desc: Twin-engine assault aircraft with a 57 mm Ho-401 cannon for tank and bomber destruction; few built.

light_bomber.name: Ki-48 Lily
light_bomber.desc: Fast twin-engine light bomber that proved vulnerable to fighters.

bomber.name: Ki-67 Hiryu
bomber.desc: Considered the best Japanese bomber; could carry a torpedo or 800 kg of bombs.

heavy_bomber.name: Ki-91 Heavy Bomber
heavy_bomber.desc: Four-engine bomber planned to match the B-17; the prototype was not completed before surrender.

stealth_bomber.name: Nakajima G10N Fugaku
stealth_bomber.desc: Six-engine bomber intended to hit US cities from Japan; never built.

diver.name: Fukuryu Diver
diver.desc: Crawling Dragon suicide divers waited under water for landing craft and detonated a pole mine against them.

patrol_boat.name: Shinyo Suicide Boat
patrol_boat.desc: Plywood motorboat carrying a 250 kg charge. Thousands were built for the home defense.

gunboat.name: Hashidate Gunboat
gunboat.desc: River gunboat designed for the China coast, with light guns and MGs.

missile_boat.name: Otori Torpedo Boat
missile_boat.desc: 1937 class with 12 cm guns and three torpedo tubes, fast but fragile.

destroyer.name: Fubuki Destroyer
destroyer.desc: First 'Special Type' destroyer with six 12.7 cm guns and nine torpedo tubes; fast and powerful for its day.

cruiser.name: Takao Heavy Cruiser
cruiser.desc: Ten 20 cm guns and 16 torpedo tubes in a 13,000 t hull; fast and formidable at night.

battleship.name: Yamato
battleship.desc: Largest battleship ever built: nine 46 cm guns and 410 mm armor. Sunk in April 1945 after air attack.

submarine.name: I-400 Submarine
submarine.desc: Largest pre-nuclear submarine, with three Aichi M6A seaplane bombers and eight torpedo tubes.

aircraft_carrier.name: Shokaku Carrier
aircraft_carrier.desc: Pearl Harbor veteran with up to 84 aircraft; sunk in June 1944 at the Philippine Sea.

mg_turret.name: Type 92 MG Nest
mg_turret.desc: Heavy 7.7 mm MG in a log-and-coconut bunker.

pillbox.name: Cave Pillbox
pillbox.desc: Reinforced cave positions with interlocking fields of fire, as at Iwo Jima.

at_gun.name: Type 1 47 mm AT Gun
at_gun.desc: Effective against Shermans at short range; Japan's best AT gun but with too few shells.

cannon_turret.name: Hillside Casemate
cannon_turret.desc: 75 mm gun in a hillside cave with a steel door; hard to find, hard to hit.

mortar_pit.name: Type 97 81 mm Mortar
mortar_pit.desc: Light mortar well hidden in caves and reverse slopes.

flak_battery.name: Type 96 25 mm AA
flak_battery.desc: Standard 25 mm AA gun; fed by 15-round magazines and slow-firing.

heavy_battery.name: Type 96 15 cm Howitzer
heavy_battery.desc: Standard Japanese medium howitzer; 15 cm shell out to 11 km.

railgun.name: 41 cm Coastal Gun
railgun.desc: Large-caliber coastal artillery, with turret and ammunition lifts similar to those on a battleship.

ciws.name: Type 96 Triple 25 mm
ciws.desc: Three 25 mm guns on one mount, the main light AA weapon of the fleet and coastal forts.

interceptor_battery.name: Type 88 AA Barrage
interceptor_battery.desc: Concentrated 75 mm AA guns firing a barrage against incoming rockets and aircraft.

abm_battery.name: Type 3 12 cm AA Gun
abm_battery.desc: 12 cm AA gun reaching 13 km; there were few and the Japanese lacked radar directors for them.

barricade.name: Log Barricade
barricade.desc: Coconut-log barricades and wire used on the island beaches.

repair_depot.name: Field Workshop
repair_depot.desc: Mobile workshop with tools and spare parts.

coastal_battery.name: 15 cm Coastal Battery
coastal_battery.desc: Coast defense guns in concrete casemates covering the beaches and harbors.

tactical_missile.name: I-Go Type 1-A
tactical_missile.desc: Radio-guided glide bomb (Ki-148), built in small numbers and not used in combat.

cruise_missile.name: Fu-Go Balloon Bomb
cruise_missile.desc: Hydrogen balloons carrying incendiary and anti-personnel bombs across the Pacific to North America.

cluster_missile.name: Type 4 20 cm Barrage
cluster_missile.desc: Barrage of 20 cm rockets fired from caves and reverse slopes.

bunker_buster.name: Type 99 No. 80 AP Bomb
bunker_buster.desc: 800 kg bomb made from battleship shells; used at Pearl Harbor against USS Arizona.

ballistic_missile.name: V-2 Derived Rocket
ballistic_missile.desc: Never built; what-if weapon. Japan received V-2 plans by submarine but built nothing like it.

hypersonic.name: Kikka Jet Strike
hypersonic.desc: Nakajima Kikka was Japan's first jet; one prototype flew in Aug 1945 as an experimental attack plane.

tactical_nuke.name: Ni-Go Fission Bomb
tactical_nuke.desc: Never built; what-if weapon. RIKEN's Ni-Go program under Nishina never reached a working device.

nuke.name: F-Go Fission Bomb
nuke.desc: Never built; what-if weapon. Kyoto's F-Go research lacked uranium and funding.

mega_nuke.name: F-Go Super Bomb
mega_nuke.desc: Never built; what-if weapon. Pure fiction for game balance.

british_army.name: British Army
british_army.desc: A small professional force built for NATO's flanks: excellent infantry, long-range precision fires and a high-end navy. No super-heavy tank, strategic bomber, battleship or coastal missile units, and cluster munitions are banned by treaty.

combined_arms.name: Combined Arms
combined_arms.desc: Balanced armor and infantry at a discount. Starts with a mixed task force.

fortress_britain.name: Fortress Britain
fortress_britain.desc: An air-defense umbrella. Starts with SAMs, CIWS and interceptors.

naval_supremacy.name: Royal Navy Supremacy
naval_supremacy.desc: Rule the waves. Starts with warships and cheaper fleet.

rifleman.name: L85A3 Rifleman
rifleman.desc: Bullpup 5.56 mm rifle with SUSAT/ACOG optic; heavily reworked after early reliability problems and now an accurate, reliable weapon.

assault.name: L22A2 Carbine Trooper
assault.desc: Short-barrel SA80 carbine, compact for vehicle crews and urban work.

bazooka.name: NLAW Team
bazooka.desc: Disposable, predicted-line-of-sight ATGM with top-attack mode; used in large numbers against Russian armor in Ukraine.

manpads.name: Starstreak HVM Team
manpads.desc: Laser-beam-riding missile releasing three tungsten darts at Mach 3+. Also fired from vehicles and ships.

mg_gunner.name: L7A2 GPMG Gunner
mg_gunner.desc: 'Gimpy': belt-fed 7.62 mm, the section's fire support weapon since the 1960s.

grenadier.name: L17A2 UGL Grenadier
grenadier.desc: Under-barrel 40 mm launcher; HEDP round defeats light armor.

sniper.name: L115A3 Long Range Rifle
sniper.desc: Accuracy International rifle in .338 Lapua Magnum; confirmed kills at 2,475 m in Afghanistan, 2009.

flamer.name: Carl Gustaf M3 HEDP Gunner
flamer.desc: 84 mm Carl Gustaf with HEDP, thermobaric and HE rounds for bunker busting; the UK retired flamethrowers long ago.

medic.name: RAMC Combat Medic
medic.desc: Trained to ATLS/BATLS standard; keeps the section on its feet in contact.

engineer.name: Royal Engineers Sapper
engineer.desc: Breaching, route clearance and repair; Royal Engineers are considered the best in NATO at explosive clearance.

commando.name: SAS Operator
commando.desc: 22 SAS: selection is among the hardest in the world. Suppressed L119A2 carbines and night vision.

jeep.name: Land Rover Wolf
jeep.desc: Defender-derived Wolf with a roof-mounted GPMG; the Army's light patrol truck for decades.

armored_car.name: Jackal 2 MWMIK
armored_car.desc: Fast, lightly protected 4x4 with a .50 HMG or Mk19 launcher; devised for Helmand patrols.

apc.name: Warrior CSP IFV
apc.desc: Tracked IFV with a 40 mm CTA cannon after its upgrade; ordered for withdrawal and being replaced by Boxer.

light_tank.name: Scimitar Mk 2 CVR(T)
light_tank.desc: Light aluminium-armored tracked scout with a 30 mm L21 RARDEN cannon; fast and low.

tank.name: Challenger 2
tank.desc: Dorchester (Chobham 2nd gen) armored MBT with 120 mm rifled L30A1 gun; never lost to enemy fire in combat before Ukraine.

heavy_tank.name: Challenger 3
heavy_tank.desc: Challenger 2 rebuilt with a Rheinmetall 120 mm L55A1 smoothbore, Trophy APS and new turret; deliveries from 2027.

tank_destroyer.name: Exactor (Spike NLOS) Launcher
tank_destroyer.desc: Spike NLOS missiles from a protected vehicle; fire-and-forget over 25 km with a top-attack seeker.

flame_tank.name: Trojan AVRE
flame_tank.desc: Challenger 2-based engineer vehicle with a 165 mm L9 demolition gun; shatters bunkers and bridges obstacles.

artillery.name: AS-90 Braveheart
artillery.desc: 155 mm/39 turreted SPG with automatic loader; burst fire of 3 rounds in 10 seconds.

howitzer.name: RCH 155
howitzer.desc: Boxer 8x8 with a remote 155 mm/52 gun and autoloader; range 40+ km. UK/German programme.

mlrs.name: M270B1 GMLRS
mlrs.desc: Tracked launcher with 12 rockets, 70+ km GPS-guided; upgraded to fire PrSM.

aa_truck.name: Stormer HVM
aa_truck.desc: Tracked Stormer with eight Starstreak ready-to-fire missiles; accompanies armor on the move.

sam_truck.name: Sky Sabre CAMM Launcher
sam_truck.desc: Common Anti-air Modular Missile on a Rapid launcher; active seeker and 25+ km range.

repair_vehicle.name: CRARRV
repair_vehicle.desc: Challenger Armoured Repair and Recovery Vehicle with crane and winch; recovers 62-ton tanks.

drone.name: Hero-120 Loitering Munition
drone.desc: Tube-launched loitering munition of the type trialled by the British Army for infantry battalions.

fighter.name: Typhoon FGR4
fighter.desc: Eurofighter Typhoon: canard-delta, supercruise-capable with Brimstone, Paveway IV and Storm Shadow.

interceptor_jet.name: Typhoon QRA (Meteor)
interceptor_jet.desc: Typhoon flown on Quick Reaction Alert with Meteor ramjet missiles (100+ km).

stealth_fighter.name: F-35B Lightning II
stealth_fighter.desc: STOVL stealth fighter with the RAF/Royal Navy; operates from HMS Queen Elizabeth. Internal weapons keep the stealth.

strike_jet.name: MQ-9B Protector RG1
strike_jet.desc: Long-endurance RPAS with Brimstone and Paveway; 40 hours loiter and SATCOM control.

helicopter.name: Wildcat AH1
helicopter.desc: Armed reconnaissance helicopter with Martlet LMM missiles and GPMG; good in littoral and ASW roles.

gunship.name: AH-64E Apache Guardian
gunship.desc: Heavy attack helicopter with Hellfire, 30 mm gun and Longbow radar; 50 for the Army Air Corps.

light_bomber.name: Tornado GR4
light_bomber.desc: Swing-wing strike aircraft retired from RAF service in 2019. Modelled as reserve stock.

stealth_bomber.name: GCAP Tempest (concept)
stealth_bomber.desc: Sixth-generation fighter-bomber planned by the UK, Italy and Japan for the mid-2030s. A modelled concept.

diver.name: Royal Marines SBS Swimmer
diver.desc: SBS combat swimmers with rebreathers and limpet mines.

patrol_boat.name: P2000 Archer-class
patrol_boat.desc: Small training/patrol boat with a 20 mm gun; used by university units and ports.

gunboat.name: River-class Batch 2 OPV
gunboat.desc: 2,000 t OPV with a 30 mm cannon; fisheries and EEZ patrol.

missile_boat.name: Type 31 Inspiration-class
missile_boat.desc: General-purpose frigate with 57 mm gun, Sea Ceptor and 24 VLS cells.

destroyer.name: Type 45 Daring-class
destroyer.desc: Sea Viper PAAMS with Aster 30 missiles; one of the best AAW ships in the world.

cruiser.name: Type 26 City-class
cruiser.desc: 6,900 t frigate with 24 Mk 41 cells and 48 CAMM silos; the RN's Tomahawk and sonar leader.

submarine.name: Astute-class
submarine.desc: Nuclear attack boat with Spearfish torpedoes and Tomahawk; very quiet.

aircraft_carrier.name: HMS Queen Elizabeth (R08)
aircraft_carrier.desc: 65,000 t STOVL carrier carrying F-35B, Merlin and Wildcat; no catapults.

mg_turret.name: L7 GPMG Sangar
mg_turret.desc: Sandbagged and Hesco sangar with a GPMG and overhead cover; typical of bases in Afghanistan.

pillbox.name: Hardened Sangar
pillbox.desc: Protected observation and fighting position made of Hesco and concrete.

at_gun.name: MILAN ATGM Post
at_gun.desc: MILAN 2 wire-guided missile with a tandem warhead; 2 km range.

cannon_turret.name: L7 105 mm Bunker
cannon_turret.desc: Fixed 105 mm L7 gun, widely produced and used in many roles.

mortar_pit.name: L16 81 mm Mortar
mortar_pit.desc: Standard British infantry mortar; 5.6 km range and fast fire.

flak_battery.name: Bofors L70 Flak
flak_battery.desc: Swedish 40 mm autocannon used by British Army Air Defence for 60 years.

sam_site.name: Rapier FSC Site
sam_site.desc: Short-range SAM with optical/radar tracking, retired 2021 but modelled as a stock.

heavy_battery.name: AS-90 155 mm Gun Battery
heavy_battery.desc: Dug-in AS-90 guns with prepared fire plans.

railgun.name: DragonFire Laser
railgun.desc: 50 kW-class laser being developed for the Royal Navy and Army; precision against drones and light targets.

ciws.name: Phalanx CIWS
ciws.desc: Land Phalanx variant used for C-RAM defense of bases in Iraq and Afghanistan.

interceptor_battery.name: Sky Sabre Battery (C-RAM)
interceptor_battery.desc: Sky Sabre with Giraffe 1X radar can also engage rockets, shells and cruise missiles.

abm_battery.name: Aster 30 B1NT Battery
abm_battery.desc: Notional land variant of the ship-borne Aster 30 B1NT; the UK relies on NATO partners.

repair_depot.name: REME Forward Repair
repair_depot.desc: Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers repair vehicles at the front.

tactical_missile.name: GMLRS Rocket
tactical_missile.desc: GPS/INS rocket with 90 kg warhead; 70+ km range.

cruise_missile.name: Tomahawk Block IV
cruise_missile.desc: Fired from RN submarines; 1,600 km range with a 450 kg warhead.

bunker_buster.name: Storm Shadow (BROACH)
bunker_buster.desc: Stealthy cruise missile with the BROACH penetrator warhead; 250 km range.

hypersonic.name: HCSW (development)
hypersonic.desc: UK/US Hypersonic Cruise Strike Weapon in development.

tactical_nuke.name: Trident II D5 (Holbrooke, sub-strategic)
tactical_nuke.desc: Single-warhead mission of the ~10 kt Holbrooke warhead; intended as a limited signal.

nuke.name: Trident II D5 (3 warheads)
nuke.desc: Submarine-launched ballistic missile; about 100 kt per warhead with multiple independent re-entry vehicles.

mega_nuke.name: Trident II D5 (full salvo)
mega_nuke.desc: A full Vanguard-class load of eight missiles with up to five warheads each.

us_army.name: US Army
us_army.desc: Expeditionary force built on air power, precision fires and logistics. Premium sensors and aircraft, thin heavy armor numbers, and the deepest strategic arsenal.

air_supremacy.name: Air Supremacy
air_supremacy.desc: Fast, cheap aircraft. Starts with fighters, a strike jet and a SAM.

arsenal.name: Arsenal of Democracy
arsenal.desc: Bigger economy and cheaper armor. Starts with an armored task force.

shock_awe.name: Shock and Awe
shock_awe.desc: Missile-heavy: cheap, fast-recharging strikes. Starts with a missile shield.

rifleman.name: M4A1 Rifleman
rifleman.desc: 5.56 mm carbine with optic and laser; the squad's baseline. Accurate to about 500 m but its small round is nearly useless against armor.

assault.name: Mk18 CQB Assaulter
assault.desc: Short-barrel 5.56 mm carbine for room clearing and urban fighting. Very high rate of fire, but ineffective past 100 m.

bazooka.name: FGM-148 Javelin Team
bazooka.desc: Fire-and-forget ATGM with top-attack profile and tandem warhead; defeats any tank roof. Slow to reload and very costly per shot.

manpads.name: FIM-92 Stinger Team
manpads.desc: Shoulder-fired infrared-homing missile; effective against helicopters and low jets to about 4 km. Needs a clear line to the target.

mg_gunner.name: M240B Machine Gunner
mg_gunner.desc: 7.62 mm belt-fed gun giving the squad suppressive fire out to 800 m. Heavy to carry, so slow to reposition.

grenadier.name: M320 Grenadier
grenadier.desc: Under-barrel 40 mm launcher firing HE and airburst rounds. Devastating on infantry in the open, weak against any armor.

sniper.name: M107 .50 Sniper
sniper.desc: Semi-automatic .50 BMG rifle with 1.8 km reach. Kills infantry instantly and can disable light vehicles, but is wasted on tanks.

flamer.name: SMAW-NE Thermobaric Gunner
flamer.desc: The US retired flamethrowers in the 1970s; the Marines' SMAW with a thermobaric round fills the bunker-clearing role today.

medic.name: 68W Combat Medic
medic.desc: Forward medic trained to TCCC standard; keeps a squad fighting through tourniquets and quick triage.

engineer.name: 12B Combat Engineer
engineer.desc: Breaches obstacles, repairs vehicles under fire and rebuilds positions with demolition and field kit.

commando.name: CAG Operator (Delta Force)
commando.desc: Highly trained assaulters with suppressed 5.56 mm rifles and night vision. Deadly and mobile, but expensive and few.

jeep.name: M1278 JLTV
jeep.desc: Joint Light Tactical Vehicle replacing the Humvee: better mine protection and payload, with a .50 cal remote station.

armored_car.name: M1117 Guardian ASV
armored_car.desc: 4x4 armored car with a Mk19 grenade launcher and .50 cal. Found in convoy security and base defense.

apc.name: M2A3 Bradley IFV
apc.desc: 25 mm Bushmaster cannon and TOW missiles with six dismounts. Tough enough to lead an assault and kill light armor.

light_tank.name: M10 Booker MPF
light_tank.desc: 105 mm Mobile Protected Firepower for infantry brigades: more mobile than an Abrams but only lightly armored.

tank.name: M1A2 SEPv3 Abrams
tank.desc: 120 mm smoothbore, composite and depleted-uranium armor and a 1,500 hp turbine. Best crew protection and fire control of its generation.

heavy_tank.name: M1A2C Abrams (Trophy APS)
heavy_tank.desc: SEPv3 fitted with the Trophy active protection system and extra armor packages, which shoot down incoming ATGMs and RPGs.

mammoth.name: M1E3 Abrams (prototype)
mammoth.desc: Proposed lighter Abrams with an autoloader, reduced crew and hybrid drive. Prototype-stage; modelled as a fast, well-armored premium tank.

tank_destroyer.name: M1134 Stryker ATGM
tank_destroyer.desc: 8x8 wheeled carrier with a twin-tube TOW 2B launcher that attacks the top of armor. Quick but thin-skinned.

flame_tank.name: M1150 Assault Breacher
flame_tank.desc: Abrams hull with a mine plow and a rocket-propelled line charge (MICLIC) that levels fortifications ahead of an assault.

artillery.name: M109A7 Paladin
artillery.desc: 155 mm tracked howitzer sharing the Bradley chassis. Accurate with GPS-guided Excalibur rounds.

howitzer.name: M1299 ERCA
howitzer.desc: 58-caliber 155 mm gun firing rocket-assisted shells out to 70 km. Experimental; hugely accurate but delicate.

mlrs.name: M142 HIMARS
mlrs.desc: Wheeled launcher firing GPS-guided GMLRS rockets with 200 kg warheads out to 70 km, then relocates before counter-fire.

aa_truck.name: M-SHORAD Stryker
aa_truck.desc: Stryker with a 30 mm cannon, Stingers and Hellfire for helicopters, drones and cruise missiles.

sam_truck.name: M901 Patriot PAC-3 MSE
sam_truck.desc: Hit-to-kill missile with a 35 km range; backbone of Western theater air and missile defense.

repair_vehicle.name: M88A2 Hercules
repair_vehicle.desc: 70-ton recovery vehicle that can tow an Abrams, lift turrets and perform field repairs under fire.

drone.name: Switchblade 600
drone.desc: Tube-launched kamikaze drone with a 40 km reach. Operators confirm the target on a live feed before the dive.

fighter.name: F-16C Block 50
fighter.desc: Single-engine light fighter with a 20 mm cannon and AIM-9/AIM-120 missiles. Cheap to fly and found everywhere.

interceptor_jet.name: F-15C Eagle
interceptor_jet.desc: Twin-engine fighter with an undefeated air-combat record; excellent radar and AIM-120s. Poor against ground targets.

stealth_fighter.name: F-22A Raptor
stealth_fighter.desc: Stealth, supercruise and thrust vectoring let it kill before it is seen. Costly to build and maintain.

strike_jet.name: A-10C Thunderbolt II
strike_jet.desc: Built around a 30 mm GAU-8 cannon and a titanium cockpit. Slow, rugged and murderous to armor, but vulnerable to modern SAMs.

helicopter.name: AH-64E Apache Guardian
helicopter.desc: Longbow radar, Hellfire/JAGM missiles and a 30 mm chain gun. Rugged and heavily armored for its class.

gunship.name: AC-130J Ghostrider
gunship.desc: Converted C-130 with a 105 mm howitzer, 30 mm cannon and precision munitions; loiters over the target for hours.

light_bomber.name: F-15E Strike Eagle
light_bomber.desc: Two-seat Eagle carrying up to 23,000 lb of weapons. Fast enough to run through defenses and drop guided bombs.

bomber.name: B-1B Lancer
bomber.desc: Variable-sweep bomber able to carry 75,000 lb at high speed and low altitude. Mach 1.2 dash.

heavy_bomber.name: B-52H Stratofortress
heavy_bomber.desc: Eight-engine bomber in service since 1955 and planned into the 2050s. Carries 70,000 lb of bombs or cruise missiles.

stealth_bomber.name: B-2A Spirit
stealth_bomber.desc: Flying-wing bomber able to penetrate dense air defenses and drop 2,000 lb JDAMs or 30,000 lb MOPs. Only 21 built.

diver.name: Navy SEAL Combat Swimmer
diver.desc: Special-warfare swimmers who place limpet charges on hulls and piers, then slip away.

patrol_boat.name: Mk VI Patrol Boat
patrol_boat.desc: 85-ft aluminum patrol boat with remote .50 cals and a 25 mm gun for coastal and riverine work.

gunboat.name: Cyclone-class PC
gunboat.desc: 170-ft patrol ship with a 25 mm gun and Griffin missiles, used by SOF and for coastal interdiction.

missile_boat.name: Independence-class LCS
missile_boat.desc: Trimaran with a 57 mm gun and modular mission packages; can carry NSM anti-ship missiles. Fast but lightly built.

destroyer.name: DDG-51 Arleigh Burke Flt III
destroyer.desc: SPY-6 radar and 96 VLS cells for Standard missiles and Tomahawks; also an excellent ASW ship.

cruiser.name: CG-47 Ticonderoga
cruiser.desc: First Aegis warship with 122 VLS cells and two 5-inch guns; the fleet's air-defense commander.

battleship.name: DDG-1000 Zumwalt
battleship.desc: Stealth hull with two 155 mm Advanced Gun Systems built for shore bombardment. Ammo supply problems limit its guns.

submarine.name: Virginia-class Block V
submarine.desc: Nuclear attack boat with Mk 48 torpedoes and Tomahawks; very quiet. The Payload Module adds 28 more missiles.

aircraft_carrier.name: USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78)
aircraft_carrier.desc: EMALS catapults and a faster sortie rate than the Nimitz class; carries ~75 aircraft and its own escorts.

mg_turret.name: M2HB .50 Gun Position
mg_turret.desc: Sandbagged Browning M2 with interlocking fields of fire. Cheap and reliable against infantry and soft vehicles.

pillbox.name: Hesco Hardpoint
pillbox.desc: Sand-filled Hesco bastion walls and concrete roof give protection from small arms and shell splinters.

at_gun.name: TOW-2B Emplacement
at_gun.desc: Wire-guided TOW 2B with top-attack warhead, range 4.5 km. Slower than Javelin but with a bigger warhead.

cannon_turret.name: M60 Turret Emplacement
cannon_turret.desc: Old M60A3 turret with a 105 mm gun on a concrete foundation. Common on forward bases as a cheap bunker.

mortar_pit.name: M252 81 mm Mortar Pit
mortar_pit.desc: Crew-served 81 mm mortar able to drop HE rounds on targets behind cover out to 5.8 km.

flak_battery.name: M-LIDS Air Defense
flak_battery.desc: 30 mm Bushmaster guns, radar and EO sensors for shooting down small drones and low aircraft.

sam_site.name: NASAMS Fire Unit
sam_site.desc: AMRAAM-ER missiles from a networked launcher; 40 km reach and good against low fliers.

heavy_battery.name: M777A2 155 mm Battery
heavy_battery.desc: Titanium-frame towed gun, 4 t, helicopter-liftable. Fires Excalibur guided shells out to 40 km.

railgun.name: ONR Electromagnetic Railgun
railgun.desc: Navy prototype launching 10 kg projectiles at Mach 7 with no explosive charge. Cancelled in 2021, still used here as an experimental fort weapon.

ciws.name: Mk 15 Phalanx CIWS
ciws.desc: Radar-guided 20 mm Gatling at 4,500 rpm; ground-mounted C-RAM variant shoots down mortars and rockets.

interceptor_battery.name: IFPC Iron Dome Battery
interceptor_battery.desc: Tamir interceptors cued by EL/M-2084 radar; shoots down rockets, mortars and cruise missiles.

abm_battery.name: THAAD Battery
abm_battery.desc: Hit-to-kill interceptors with a 200 km range and AN/TPY-2 radar; defends against theater ballistic missiles.

barricade.name: Concrete T-Wall
barricade.desc: Precast 5-ton steel-reinforced wall blocks used to channel traffic and protect against blast.

repair_depot.name: Forward Repair Activity
repair_depot.desc: Mobile maintenance bay with welders, generators and spare parts to keep vehicles in the fight.

coastal_battery.name: NMESIS Coastal Battery
coastal_battery.desc: Marine Corps launcher on an unmanned JLTV-class chassis firing Naval Strike Missiles at ships up to 185 km away.

tactical_missile.name: PrSM Increment 1
tactical_missile.desc: GPS/INS missile fired from HIMARS or M270; range over 500 km, replaces ATACMS.

cruise_missile.name: BGM-109 Tomahawk Block V
cruise_missile.desc: Subsonic land-attack missile with 1,000 lb warhead and 1,600 km range; follows terrain below radar.

cluster_missile.name: MGM-140A ATACMS (M39)
cluster_missile.desc: Carries 950 M74 bomblets over 165 km; ideal against airfields and troop concentrations.

bunker_buster.name: GBU-57 MOP
bunker_buster.desc: 30,000 lb penetrating bomb dropped from a B-2, designed to burrow deep before detonating.

ballistic_missile.name: Pershing II
ballistic_missile.desc: Cold War IRBM with a maneuvering reentry vehicle. Retired in 1991 under the INF treaty; modelled as a reactivated stock.

hypersonic.name: LRHW Dark Eagle
hypersonic.desc: Army's Common-Hypersonic Glide Body on a Navy-derived booster; Mach 5+ glide, range ~2,800 km.

tactical_nuke.name: B61-12 Guided Bomb
tactical_nuke.desc: Variable-yield (0.3-50 kt) gravity bomb with a guided tail kit; deployed in Europe.

nuke.name: LGM-30G Minuteman III
nuke.desc: Silo-based 3-stage ICBM; 13,000 km range, 300 kt W87. 400 are on alert in the US.

mega_nuke.name: B41 (Mk-41) 25 Mt Bomb
mega_nuke.desc: Highest-yield US weapon ever deployed (1960-76). A 4.8-ton gravity bomb from a B-52.

french_army.name: French Army
french_army.tagline: Fortress, legion, and force de frappe.
french_army.desc: An independent nuclear power with an expeditionary army: agile infantry, wheeled armor, a strong air force and a national deterrent. No super-heavy tank, battleship, flamethrower vehicle or cluster munitions.

maginot.name: Ligne Maginot
maginot.desc: Concrete forts everywhere. Starts with a hardened front line.

force_de_frappe.name: Force de Frappe
force_de_frappe.desc: Independent nuclear deterrent: cheap, fast-recharging strategic weapons.

legion.name: Legion Etrangere
legion.desc: Tough, cheap elite infantry. Starts with legionnaires and commandos.

rifleman.name: HK416F Fantassin
rifleman.desc: Short-stroke gas-piston 5.56 mm rifle replacing the FAMAS from 2017; far more reliable in dust and wet.

assault.name: FAMAS Felin Assaulter
assault.desc: Compact bullpup with a very high rate of fire (~1,000 rpm), still in service with units not yet re-equipped.

bazooka.name: Eryx / MMP Team
bazooka.desc: MMP (Missile Moyenne Portee) tandem-warhead ATGM with fire-and-forget or man-in-loop; 4 km range.

manpads.name: Mistral 3 Team
manpads.desc: Infrared-homing missile with 6 km range; seeker discriminates decoys well.

mg_gunner.name: Minimi / MAG 58 Gunner
mg_gunner.desc: FN Minimi 5.56 mm light machine gun for the section and MAG 58 for vehicle crews.

grenadier.name: FELIN Grenadier
grenadier.desc: FELIN soldier system with a 40 mm HK GLM launcher and integrated optics.

sniper.name: PGM Hecate II Sniper
sniper.desc: Bolt-action .50 BMG rifle with 1,800 m range; also used to destroy IEDs from afar.

flamer.name: LRAC 89 Rocket Gunner
flamer.desc: 89 mm rocket launcher with HEAT and HE rounds for fortifications; France retired flamethrowers decades ago.

medic.name: Auxiliaire Sanitaire
medic.desc: Service de Sante des Armees medic; tourniquets, hemostatic dressings and rapid evacuation.

engineer.name: Genie Combat Engineer
engineer.desc: Genie de combat: clears mines and obstacles, builds field fortifications.

commando.name: Legion Etrangere Commando
commando.desc: Foreign Legion paratroopers (2e REP) with HK416F and night vision; high endurance and discipline.

jeep.name: VBL Scout Car
jeep.desc: Light 4x4 armored reconnaissance vehicle, 3.5 t; amphibious without preparation.

armored_car.name: AMX-10 RC
armored_car.desc: Six-wheeled armored car with 105 mm gun; very fast and quiet but light armor.

apc.name: VBCI IFV
apc.desc: 8x8 wheeled IFV with 25 mm cannon; 8 dismounts. Rolls fast on roads.

light_tank.name: EBRC Jaguar
light_tank.desc: 6x6 wheeled armored recon vehicle with 40 mm CTA cannon, replacing the AMX-10 RC and ERC-90.

tank.name: Leclerc Tank
tank.desc: 120 mm smoothbore with autoloader, 3-man crew and excellent fire control; lighter than most MBTs.

heavy_tank.name: Leclerc XLR
heavy_tank.desc: Upgraded Leclerc with new sights, ERA and digital systems: more armor and a data link.

tank_destroyer.name: AMX-10 RC with MMP
tank_destroyer.desc: Wheeled platform with MMP-class guided missile, derived from AMX-10 RC.

artillery.name: AuF1 TA SPG
artillery.desc: 155 mm/40 turret on AMX-30 chassis; still in service, being replaced by CAESAR.

howitzer.name: CAESAR 155 mm
howitzer.desc: 155 mm/52 gun on a 6x6 truck chassis; shoots and scoots in under 60 seconds. Widely exported and used in Ukraine.

mlrs.name: LRU MLRS
mlrs.desc: French version of the M270 with GMLRS rockets; 70+ km range.

aa_truck.name: VAB Mistral AA
aa_truck.desc: VAB 4x4 with Mistral missile launcher; protects convoys against helicopters and drones.

sam_truck.name: VL MICA Launcher
sam_truck.desc: Vertical launch MICA IR/EM missile on a truck; 20 km range and radar guidance.

repair_vehicle.name: Leclerc DNG ARV
repair_vehicle.desc: Leclerc-based Depanneur-Niveleur with dozer blade, crane and winch.

drone.name: Larinae Loitering Munition
drone.desc: French Larinae munition from MBDA Cervus family: 40+ km reach and 3-kg warhead.

fighter.name: Rafale C
fighter.desc: Dassault Rafale: delta-canard with Meteor, Mica and SCALP-EG; ~10,000 pounds payload.

interceptor_jet.name: Mirage 2000-5
interceptor_jet.desc: Delta-wing fighter with RDY radar and MICA missiles; a pure air-defense jet.

stealth_fighter.name: nEUROn Stealth UCAV
stealth_fighter.desc: Dassault-led European UCAV demonstrator (first flight 2012); a stealth flying wing used to test the SCAF drone.

strike_jet.name: Rafale B Strike
strike_jet.desc: Two-seat Rafale B with AASM Hammer, SCALP and the nuclear ASMPA.

helicopter.name: Tigre HAP
helicopter.desc: Eurocopter Tigre support/escort variant with a 30 mm cannon and rockets.

gunship.name: Tigre HAD Gunship
gunship.desc: Tigre with Hellfire II and Mistral; heavier armament and countermeasures.

light_bomber.name: Mirage 2000D
light_bomber.desc: Mirage 2000 conversions to precision strike with Laser-guided bombs and SCALP; ageing.

bomber.name: Mirage IV Bomber
bomber.desc: Supersonic Mach 2 bomber for the nuclear force de frappe, in service 1964-2005; Reconnaissance P version to 2005.

heavy_bomber.name: Mirage IVA Strategic
heavy_bomber.desc: Strategic Mirage IV variant carrying a 60-kt AN-22 gravity bomb or the ASMP missile.

stealth_bomber.name: SCAF NGF Stealth
stealth_bomber.desc: Next-Generation Fighter of the Future Combat Air System (France, Germany, Spain); planned for the 2040s.

diver.name: Commando Hubert
diver.desc: French Navy combat swimmers (Commando Hubert) are among the world's best; mines and demolition.

patrol_boat.name: Vedette Patrol Boat
patrol_boat.desc: Fast patrol launch for coastal and port duties.

gunboat.name: Gowind OPV
gunboat.desc: 1,000 t OPV with a 20 mm gun and flight deck; economical patrol vessel.

missile_boat.name: La Fayette Frigate
missile_boat.desc: 3,600 t frigate with Exocet, Crotale and a 100 mm gun; one of the first stealth-shaped warships.

destroyer.name: FREMM Aquitaine
destroyer.desc: 6,000 t ASW/AAW frigate with 16 VLS Aster and Exocet/MdCN missiles.

cruiser.name: Horizon-class (Forbin)
cruiser.desc: 7,000 t PAAMS destroyer with 48 VLS cells; Europe's top AAW surface ships.

submarine.name: Barracuda (Suffren)
submarine.desc: 4,700 t nuclear attack sub with F21 torpedoes and MdCN cruise missiles.

aircraft_carrier.name: Charles de Gaulle (R91)
aircraft_carrier.desc: 42,000 t nuclear-powered carrier with catapults and ~40 aircraft; the only non-US nuclear carrier.

mg_turret.name: AAT-52 MG Nest
mg_turret.desc: 7.62 mm AAT-52 on tripod in a fortified position.

pillbox.name: Maginot Pillbox
pillbox.desc: Maginot Line petit ouvrage: armored cloche with MGs behind thick concrete.

at_gun.name: MMP ATGM Post
at_gun.desc: Fixed MMP launcher with 4 km range and a tandem warhead.

cannon_turret.name: Maginot Casemate
cannon_turret.desc: 47 mm turret and 75 mm casemate guns in the Maginot Line.

mortar_pit.name: MO-120-RT Mortar
mortar_pit.desc: 120 mm rifled mortar with 8 km range; more accurate than smoothbore tubes.

flak_battery.name: Tarasque 20 mm AA
flak_battery.desc: Fast-firing 20 mm cannon on a mobile mount; used against low-flying aircraft and drones.

sam_site.name: Crotale NG SAM
sam_site.desc: All-weather short-range SAM with radar and IR; 11 km.

heavy_battery.name: TRF1 155 mm Battery
heavy_battery.desc: Towed 155 mm/40 TRF1 howitzer; 24 km, long in service.

railgun.name: ISL Railgun Battery
railgun.desc: Franco-German ISL research railgun test fixture; reached 8 MJ muzzle energy.

ciws.name: Simbad Mistral CIWS
ciws.desc: Twin Mistral launcher for close defence, used on ships and ground sites.

interceptor_battery.name: SAMP/T Battery
interceptor_battery.desc: Aster 30 missiles with Arabel radar; 100 km range, Mach 4.5.

abm_battery.name: SAMP/T NG
abm_battery.desc: Upgraded SAMP/T with Aster 30 B1NT and Ground Fire radar to counter ballistic missiles.

barricade.name: Hedgehog Barrier
barricade.desc: Czech hedgehog steel barrier; tough against vehicles.

repair_depot.name: Atelier Mobile
repair_depot.desc: Mobile maintenance for armor and artillery.

coastal_battery.name: Exocet MM40 Battery
coastal_battery.desc: Truck-mounted Exocet MM40 Block 3: 200 km sea-skimming missile.

tactical_missile.name: Hades Tactical
tactical_missile.desc: 480 km ballistic missile (retired 1997); modelled as stock.

cruise_missile.name: SCALP-EG
cruise_missile.desc: Stealthy long-range 450 km cruise missile with 450 kg warhead.

bunker_buster.name: AASM Hammer
bunker_buster.desc: 250 kg modular bomb with GPS/INS and IR seeker, ranges 70 km.

ballistic_missile.name: S3D Plateau d'Albion
ballistic_missile.desc: Silo-based two-stage IRBM carrying a 1.2 Mt warhead, in service 1980-96; modelled as reactivated stock.

hypersonic.name: ASN4G Hypersonic
hypersonic.desc: Future nuclear ASN4G ramjet/ hypersonic; planned.

tactical_nuke.name: ASMPA TN 81
tactical_nuke.desc: Nuclear cruise missile with TNA warhead 300 kt; Rafale/Mirage.

nuke.name: M51 SLBM
nuke.desc: M51 submarine-launched ballistic missile with six TNO warheads of 100 kt, 10,000 km range.

italian_army.name: Italian Royal Army
italian_army.desc: Regio Esercito and Regia Marina: elegant, brave and underfunded. Fast Bersaglieri, fine guns (the 90/53) and a good navy, but light, poorly armored tanks and few aircraft. No rocket artillery, drones, helicopters, super-heavy tank or stealth bomber; the nuclear slots are what-ifs.

ariete.name: Ariete Armoured
ariete.desc: Light fast armor and armored cars. Starts with a mobile column.

alpini.name: Alpini Mountain Defense
alpini.desc: Dug-in alpine strongpoints. Starts with pillboxes, AT guns and mortars.

regia_marina.name: Regia Marina
regia_marina.desc: Mediterranean sea power. Starts with a small fleet.

rifleman.name: Carcano M91/38 Bersagliere
rifleman.desc: 6.5 mm Carcano: light, accurate and cheap but low-powered. Bersaglieri are fast infantry with plumed helmets.

assault.name: Beretta MAB 38A SMG
assault.desc: Well-made 9 mm SMG with a 40-round magazine; widely admired and used by the Germans too.

bazooka.name: Solothurn 20 mm AT Rifle
bazooka.desc: Semi-automatic 20 mm anti-tank rifle with a 20 mm round; penetrates light tanks only.

manpads.name: Breda 20 mm AA Gunner
manpads.desc: Breda Mod. 35 20 mm autocannon on a wheeled mount, mainly the army's AA defense.

mg_gunner.name: Breda 30 LMG Gunner
mg_gunner.desc: 6.5 mm LMG with a 20-round fixed magazine; sensitive to dirt and dust.

grenadier.name: SRCM Mod. 35 Grenadier
grenadier.desc: Small red SRCM grenades: handy but weak; supplemented by rifle grenades.

sniper.name: Carcano Cecchino
sniper.desc: Carcano with a telescopic sight, used by selected marksmen on the Alpine front.

flamer.name: Lanciafiamme Mod. 35
flamer.desc: Italian backpack flamethrower used by assault engineers against bunkers.

medic.name: Sanitari Medic
medic.desc: Stretcher-bearers and sanitari with bandages and morphine.

engineer.name: Genio Sapper
engineer.desc: Genio engineers lay mines, build bridges and demolish obstacles.

commando.name: Folgore Paratrooper
commando.desc: The Folgore Division fought to the last at El Alamein; the Brits called them the best Axis troops there.

jeep.name: Fiat 508 CM Coloniale
jeep.desc: Small scout car based on the Balilla; a few with MG mounts.

armored_car.name: AB 41 Autoblinda
armored_car.desc: Eight-wheeled armored car with a 20 mm Breda and reversible driver; good desert scout.

apc.name: AS 42 Sahariana
apc.desc: Light desert patrol truck with a 20 mm AT gun or MGs; fast in sand.

light_tank.name: L6/40 Light Tank
light_tank.desc: Light tank with a 20 mm Breda cannon; not good against anything heavier.

tank.name: M13/40 Medium Tank
tank.desc: Riveted 14-ton tank with a 47 mm gun; poor armor and slow, but with decent engine.

heavy_tank.name: P26/40 Heavy Tank
heavy_tank.desc: Italy's best tank design: 26 t with a 75/34 gun and 60 mm armor. Only a handful were completed.

tank_destroyer.name: Semovente 90/53
tank_destroyer.desc: M41 chassis with the dual-purpose 90/53 gun; deadly but very rare (~30 built).

flame_tank.name: L3 Flame Tankette
flame_tank.desc: Tiny CV 33 tankette with a flamethrower and fuel trailer.

artillery.name: Semovente 75/18
artillery.desc: Compact SPG with a short 75 mm howitzer: very good at supporting infantry.

howitzer.name: Cannone 149/40 Mod. 35
howitzer.desc: Heavy field gun with 23 km range; towed by tractor.

aa_truck.name: Breda 20/65 AA Truck
aa_truck.desc: Breda 20 mm cannon on a truck for mobile air defense.

sam_truck.name: Autocannone 90/53
sam_truck.desc: Heavy AA 90/53 cannon on Lancia 3Ro truck; the famed gun also fires against tanks.

repair_vehicle.name: Recovery Tractor
repair_vehicle.desc: Heavy tractor with winch used to recover tanks and guns.

fighter.name: Macchi C.202 Folgore
fighter.desc: Italian fighter with a German DB 601 engine; agile and well-liked, but armed with only machine guns.

interceptor_jet.name: Macchi C.205 Veltro
interceptor_jet.desc: Improved C.202 with two 20 mm cannons and 12.7 mm MGs.

stealth_fighter.name: Reggiane Re.2005 Sagittario
stealth_fighter.desc: Probably the best Italian fighter of the war, with 20 mm cannons; few were built.

strike_jet.name: Breda Ba.65
strike_jet.desc: Single-engine attack monoplane; slow and lightly armored.

gunship.name: Breda Ba.88 Lince
gunship.desc: Twin-engined attack aircraft that performed disastrously; used as decoys on airfields.

light_bomber.name: SM.79 Sparviero
light_bomber.desc: Three-engine bomber and torpedo bomber, nicknamed 'hunchback'.

bomber.name: Cant Z.1007bis Alcione
bomber.desc: Three-engine wooden medium bomber, good load but vulnerable.

heavy_bomber.name: Piaggio P.108B
heavy_bomber.desc: Four-engine heavy bomber (Italy's only one); about 160 km/h slower than the B-17.

diver.name: Decima MAS Frogman
diver.desc: X MAS combat swimmers sank multiple British ships at Alexandria with 'maiale' human torpedoes.

patrol_boat.name: MAS Torpedo Boat
patrol_boat.desc: Fast MAS boat with two torpedoes and a 20 mm gun.

gunboat.name: Cannoniera Gunboat
gunboat.desc: Small coastal gunboat with 76 mm gun.

missile_boat.name: MTM Explosive Boat
missile_boat.desc: Barchino explosive motorboat: the pilot steers it at the target and bails out. Sank HMS York at Suda Bay, 1941.
